Strand: Creation 1.2 Marriage and Family (4 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the 
Topic 1.3: Leisure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Leisure. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can youths avoid misuse of leisure time?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest
2. explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure
3. describe how youths misuse leisure time today
4. identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LEISURE
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Leisure helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: LEISURE
Study Leisure like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leisure” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure

What this means
In this part you learn to explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leisure in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe how youths misuse leisure time today

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how youths misuse leisure time today. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how youths misuse leisure time today.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how youths misuse leisure time today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time

What this means
In this part you learn to identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leisure” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Leisure is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Leisure” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leisure in your own words. (skill: explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: describe how youths misuse leisure time today)

Example 4: Show how “Leisure” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Leisure to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest.
3. Practise this skill: explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure.
4. Practise this skill: describe how youths misuse leisure time today.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Leisure from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Leisure: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Leisure?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can youths avoid misuse of leisure time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Leisure means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the biblical teaching on God’s rest.
5. Be able to: explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
